testCase.title: Scissor stair counted as two exits

projectContext.occupancy: Group R-2 stated by the question
projectContext.configuration: Scissor stair with entrance doors 15 feet apart

exactPassages: Stairs sharing any common wall, floor, ceiling, scissor stair assembly, or other enclosure shall be counted as one exit stairway.

3. Group R-2 occupancies. In Group R-2 occupancies, where stairs are enclosed in walls having at least a 2-hour fire resistance rating and constructed of masonry or masonry equivalent in accordance with department rules: 3.1. The exit doors to such stairs shall be placed a distance apart equal to no less than 15 feet (4572 mm); and 3.2. Such stairs shall be permitted to share common walls, floors, ceilings or scissor stairs assemblies or other enclosures provided that the construction separating the stairs is also of at least a 2-hour fire-resistance rating and constructed of masonry or masonry equivalent in accordance with department rules.

testCase.question: Our Group R-2 building has a scissor stair with the two stair entrance doors located 15 feet apart. Can the two stairs be counted as two separate exits?
testCase.expectedConclusion: The 15-foot separation alone is not enough. Under the general rule, stairs sharing a scissor-stair assembly are counted as one exit stairway. However, the Group R-2 exception permits the stairs to share the assembly and be counted separately when the stair enclosures and the construction separating the stairs have at least a 2-hour fire-resistance rating and are constructed of masonry or a masonry equivalent in accordance with department rules. The exit doors must also be at least 15 feet apart. Confirm the occupancy group, enclosure rating, separating construction, and material before concluding that the exception applies.

answer.conclusion: No definitive affirmative determination can be made from the selected passages alone. The general rule expressly states that stairs sharing a scissor stair assembly (or any common wall, floor, ceiling, or enclosure) “shall be counted as one exit stairway.” [§ 1007.1.1, Passage 9cd0c975-6625-42a4-9dfb-bd59e8cdb710] The R-2 provision permits qualifying stairs to share a scissor stair assembly or other enclosure when specified fire-resistance and masonry conditions are met, and it requires the exit doors to be at least 15 feet apart. [§ 1007.1.1, Passage b4eef08a-f305-4513-b304-dda29783539b] However, the supplied R-2 text does not expressly state that qualifying shared/scissor stairs are to be counted as two separate exit stairways, nor does the supplied excerpt show the scope or introductory language establishing whether Item 3 overrides the general counting sentence. If the full provision establishes Item 3 as an exception to the counting rule, the two stairs may be countable separately only when all of that item’s conditions are satisfied; that override cannot be confirmed from these excerpts alone.
answer.explanation: A 15-foot door separation satisfies the stated minimum door-separation threshold because the R-2 provision requires a distance of “no less than 15 feet.” [§ 1007.1.1, Passage b4eef08a-f305-4513-b304-dda29783539b] But door separation is not the only stated condition. The R-2 language also requires the stair enclosure walls to have at least a 2-hour fire-resistance rating and be constructed of masonry or masonry equivalent under department rules. It further permits shared walls, floors, ceilings, scissor assemblies, or other enclosures only where the construction separating the stairs also has at least a 2-hour rating and is masonry or masonry equivalent under department rules. [§ 1007.1.1, Passage b4eef08a-f305-4513-b304-dda29783539b] In contrast, the general selected sentence expressly directs that shared scissor stairs be counted as one exit stairway. [§ 1007.1.1, Passage 9cd0c975-6625-42a4-9dfb-bd59e8cdb710]

testCase.title: Occupancy classification of a residential multipurpose room

exactPassages: A room or space used for assembly purposes with an occupant load of fewer than 75 persons and accessory to another occupancy shall be classified as a Group B occupancy or as part of that occupancy, except that the number of plumbing fixtures for such a room or space is permitted to be calculated in accordance with the requirements for assembly occupancies.

For areas without fixed seating, the occupant load shall be not less than that number determined by dividing the floor area under consideration by the occupant load factor assigned to the function of the space as set forth in Table 1004.1.3.

testCase.question: A 900-net-square-foot multipurpose room in an apartment building will normally contain tables and chairs and is only for residents. Does it need to be classified as Group A-3?
testCase.expectedConclusion: For an unconcentrated assembly arrangement with tables and chairs, Table 1004.1.3 uses 15 net square feet per occupant. A 900-net-square-foot room therefore has a calculated occupant load of 60 people. Because that is fewer than 75 occupants, and assuming the room is accessory to the residential occupancy, BC 303.1.3 permits it to be classified as Group B or as part of the occupancy it serves rather than as Group A. The result depends on the actual net area, furniture arrangement, intended activities, and whether the room is truly accessory to the residential use.

Calculate 900 divided by 15 as an occupant load of 60.

Avoid automatically classifying every residential amenity room as Group R-2.
missingFacts: Confirm the actual net area.

answer.conclusion: No—based on the selected provisions, the room would not need to be classified as Group A-3 if it is an assembly-purpose space accessory to the apartment building’s other occupancy. A 900-net-square-foot area with unconcentrated tables and chairs produces an occupant load of 60 persons (900 ÷ 15 net), which is fewer than 75. Section 303.1.3 therefore directs that it be classified as Group B or as part of the occupancy to which it is accessory, rather than as Group A-3. The selected evidence does not establish which of those two classifications applies in this particular building. (SECTION_ID 132, PASSAGE_ID 3d56edb9-9692-433e-a78f-4c6045260049; SECTION_ID 2152, PASSAGE_IDs 4ffb9602-1629-4cfe-afa4-60033245f089, 8b3b6dd6-a28f-40b4-b7fa-46c43fa6c17a, 3315c53a-9d27-48b6-b08d-de5382434af8.)
answer.explanation:
For an area without fixed seating, occupant load is determined by dividing the floor area by the Table 1004.1.3 factor assigned to the space’s function. The selected table entries identify “Unconcentrated (tables and chairs)” at 15 net. Thus: 900 net square feet ÷ 15 net square feet/person = 60 persons. (SECTION_ID 2152, PASSAGE_IDs 4ffb9602-1629-4cfe-afa4-60033245f089, 8b3b6dd6-a28f-40b4-b7fa-46c43fa6c17a, 3315c53a-9d27-48b6-b08d-de5382434af8.)

Section 303.1.3 applies where a room or space is used for assembly purposes, has an occupant load fewer than 75 persons, and is accessory to another occupancy. It classifies that space as Group B or as part of the occupancy to which it is accessory, while allowing its plumbing-fixture count to be calculated under assembly-occupancy requirements. (SECTION_ID 132, PASSAGE_ID 3d56edb9-9692-433e-a78f-4c6045260049.)

testCase.title: Plumbing fixtures for an accessory assembly space

projectContext.potentialClassification: Group B under the accessory assembly provision

exactPassages: A room or space used for assembly purposes with an occupant load of fewer than 75 persons and accessory to another occupancy shall be classified as a Group B occupancy or as part of that occupancy, except that the number of plumbing fixtures for such a room or space is permitted to be calculated in accordance with the requirements for assembly occupancies.

Plumbing fixtures shall be provided for the type of occupancy and in the minimum number shown in Table 403.1. Types of occupancies not shown in Table 403.1 shall be considered individually by the commissioner. The number of occupants shall be determined by the New York City Building Code. Occupancy classification shall be determined in accordance with the New York City Building Code.

The number of fixtures for building or nonaccessory tenant space used for assembly purposes by fewer than 75 persons and classified as Group B occupancy in accordance with Section 303.1, Exception 2 of the New York City Building Code shall be permitted to be calculated in accordance with the requirements for Assembly occupancies.

To determine the occupant load of each sex, the total occupant load shall be divided in half. To determine the required number of fixtures, the fixture ratio or ratios for each fixture type shall be applied to the occupant load of each sex in accordance with Table 403.1. Fractional numbers resulting from applying the fixture ratios of Table 403.1 shall be rounded up to the next whole number. For calculations involving multiple occupancies, such fractional numbers for each occupancy shall first be summed and then rounded up to the next whole number. Fixture calculations in Group B office occupancies shall utilize the total occupant load on a given floor to determine the number of fixtures required for that floor.
Exception: The total occupant load shall not be required to be divided in half where approved statistical data indicates a distribution of the sexes of other than 50 percent of each sex.

testCase.question: If the multipurpose room is permitted to be classified as Group B because it has fewer than 75 occupants, can its required plumbing fixtures be calculated using the normal Group B fixture requirements?
testCase.expectedConclusion: Not automatically. Although an accessory assembly space with fewer than 75 occupants may be classified as Group B or as part of the occupancy it serves, the code permits the plumbing fixtures for that assembly use to be calculated using the applicable Assembly fixture requirements. The appropriate assembly category must first be identified from the room's actual use. The total occupant load is generally divided equally between the sexes unless approved statistical information supports another distribution. Fixture ratios are then applied, fractions are combined as required for multiple occupancies, and the resulting fractions are rounded up. A final fixture count requires the calculated occupant load, applicable assembly use, existing shared facilities, and other relevant project conditions.

answer.conclusion: Not necessarily. If the multipurpose room qualifies under BC §303.1.3—i.e., it is used for assembly purposes, has an occupant load of fewer than 75 persons, and is accessory to another occupancy—it may be classified as Group B (or part of the other occupancy). However, both BC §303.1.3 and PC §403.1 expressly permit its plumbing-fixture count to be calculated under the Assembly-occupancy requirements. Thus, Group B classification does not require use of the normal Group B fixture calculation; Assembly fixture requirements are an expressly permitted alternative for a qualifying room. The selected provisions do not establish that Assembly calculations are mandatory or prohibit normal Group B calculations. [BC §303.1.3, PASSAGE_ID adf941a1-aa0e-45ad-81bf-c89fdac171a9; PC §403.1, PASSAGE_ID 78a7a44f-0bb6-41a0-8c35-ada9ca1b1674]
answer.explanation:
PC §403.1 generally requires fixtures based on the occupancy classification determined under the Building Code and the occupant load determined by the Building Code. For a qualifying accessory assembly room with fewer than 75 occupants that is classified as Group B, the Building Code specifically states that its fixture number is permitted to be calculated using Assembly requirements. The Plumbing Code repeats that permission for qualifying assembly space classified as Group B. [PC §403.1, PASSAGE_ID 8a940d19-d3e6-4c7b-921d-233b5a4faa05; BC §303.1.3, PASSAGE_ID adf941a1-aa0e-45ad-81bf-c89fdac171a9; PC §403.1, PASSAGE_ID 78a7a44f-0bb6-41a0-8c35-ada9ca1b1674]

If a fixture calculation is made, the selected evidence states that Table 403.1 ratios are applied by sex, fractions are generally rounded up, and calculations involving multiple occupancies require fractional results for each occupancy to be summed before rounding. A different sex distribution may be used where approved statistical data supports it. [PC §403.1.1, PASSAGE_ID 9c58b798-c73e-4335-abed-08a86518a6b3; PC §403.1.1 Exception, PASSAGE_ID 4e4d1257-413c-4ca9-bebf-1810e6a7718a]
